I broke my femur in a motorcycle accident when I was 15. The accident happened on July 9th.

I was in traction for 12 weeks with a 1/4" threaded rod screwed right through my femur bone above the knee joint. There was about 1" to 1-1/2" inches of rod sticking out each side of my leg. (That's where they attached the apparatus to keep my leg in traction.)

I lived in a small town at the time and had to be in a hospital in a different city about an hour away. My parents came to visit for a few hours on Sunday afternoons (but didn't make it every weekend). My so-called friends visited me once the entire 12 weeks.

I laid on my back that entire time. No computers, no cell phones, 4 channels on a black-and-white TV. When my leg sufficiently healed I was then put in a cast for another 12-1/2 weeks. The cast was from just below my chest down my right let with only my toes showing.

When I finally got the cast off my leg muscles atrophied so much that I had larger muscles in my arms. It took weeks of painful exercise for me build the muscles back up and to learn to walk without crutches. It took many more months to learn to walk without a limp.

That experience changed my entire outlook on life. I became more focused on what I wanted out of life and learned to stop feeling so sorry for myself. Turned out to be one of the best experiences of my life.
